summary.en: The 92‑year-old federal judge overseeing the Maduro drug-trafficking case has died and a new judge has been appointed as Maduro returns to federal court to face torture allegations. A soldier who allegedly bet $400,000 on Maduro’s removal has been arrested, and another soldier is under investigation for insider trading on Polymarket. Explosive attacks near the Colombia-Venezuela border injured police officers and civilians in two separate blasts. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2007.
summary.nb: Den 92‑år gamle føderale dommeren som hadde ansvaret for Maduro-saken om narkotikasmugling, er død, og en ny dommer er utnevnt mens Maduro vender tilbake til føderal domstol for å møte anklager om tortur. En soldat som angivelig satset 400 000 $ på at Maduro skulle fjernes, er arrestert, og en annen soldat er under etterforskning for innsidehandel på Polymarket. Eksplosive angrep nær grensen mellom Colombia og Venezuela såret politifolk og sivile i to separate eksplosjoner. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2007.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
